claim_boundary: This pilot owns the versioned rule-proof schema, typed model, generator/checker, and a sixteen-rule cohort (#6973 pilot, #17661 cohort 2, cohort 3). It does not migrate the remaining 12 native rules, absorb #6978 variable/scope proof, or change critic rule semantics.

cases.proposition: A file without use strict emits one insertion-range finding with a Safe automatic-candidate edit; applying it reparses and removes the target diagnostic.
An independently authored shebang-plus-package file that does use strict is not a missing-pragma finding.
use Test2::V0 satisfies require_use_strict without a bare use strict line.
File-level ## no critic for the governed rule suppresses the missing-strict finding; stripping it restores that same rule.
A commented use strict is not a pragma; the missing-strict finding remains rather than inheriting a clean pass from comment text.
A file without use warnings emits one insertion-range finding with a Safe automatic-candidate edit; applying it reparses and removes the target diagnostic.
An independently authored shebang-plus-package file that does use warnings is not a missing-pragma finding.
use Test2::V0 satisfies require_use_warnings without a bare use warnings line.
File-level ## no critic for the governed rule suppresses the missing-warnings finding; stripping it restores that same rule.
A commented use warnings is not a pragma; the missing-warnings finding remains rather than inheriting a clean pass from comment text.
Assignment in an if condition is a preview-candidate finding at the assignment span, never automatic.
An independently authored comparison condition is not an assignment-in-condition finding.
Double-parenthesized assignment is treated as intentional and is not a finding.
File-level suppression of the governed assignment rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented assignment-in-condition is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.
A printf with two format specifiers and one argument is a diagnostic-only arity finding at the call span.
An independently authored printf whose specifier and argument counts match is not an arity finding.
A project-shaped helper returning a matching sprintf is not an arity finding.
File-level suppression of the governed printf rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented printf arity mismatch is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.
defined @array is a preview-candidate deprecated finding at the call span, never automatic.
An independently authored defined $scalar check is not a deprecated-defined finding.
A project-shaped helper that tests an array in boolean context is not a deprecated-defined finding.
File-level suppression of the governed deprecated-defined rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented defined @array is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.

expected_findings.fix_title: Convert to three-argument open() for safety

cases.proposition: Two-argument open is a preview-candidate security finding at the call span, never automatic.
An independently authored three-argument open is not a two-argument-open finding.
A project-shaped loader using three-argument open with an error check is not a two-argument-open finding.
File-level suppression of the governed two-argument-open rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented two-argument open is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.
String eval is a diagnostic-only security finding and cannot be represented as automatic success.
Block eval is an independently authored near miss and is not a string-eval finding.
Project-shaped exception-handling block eval is not a string-eval finding.
File-level suppression of the governed string-eval rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented string eval is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.
Using $1 with no preceding match is a strict-only diagnostic-only semantic finding.
An independently authored capture after a successful match is not a finding.
A project-shaped helper that reads $1 only after a match is not a finding.
File-level suppression of the governed capture rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A single-quoted '$1' is not a capture-variable use; string text does not inherit a positive.
Checking $@ in the statement after an unlocalized block eval is a diagnostic-only stale-error finding at the $@ span.
An independently authored block that localizes $@ before eval is not a stale-error finding.
A project-shaped helper that checks the eval return value instead of $@ is not a stale-error finding.
File-level suppression of the governed stale-error rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented eval/$@ check is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.
A statement after an unconditional return is an automatic-candidate unreachable finding; removing the line reparses and removes the target.
An independently authored conditional return leaves the following statement reachable and is not a finding.
A project-shaped helper with a conditional early return and a reachable eval is not an unreachable finding.
File-level suppression of the governed unreachable rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented statement after a return is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.
open with a bareword handle is a preview-candidate finding at the handle span, never automatic.
An independently authored lexical-handle open is not a bareword-filehandle finding.
A project-shaped loader that opens a lexical handle with or die is not a bareword-filehandle finding.
File-level suppression of the governed bareword rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A standard filehandle (STDOUT) is exempt and is not a bareword-filehandle finding.
A three-argument pipe open is a diagnostic-only pipe-open finding at the call span.
An independently authored plain file open is not a pipe-open finding.
A project-shaped loader that opens a plain file with or die is not a pipe-open finding.
File-level suppression of the governed pipe-open rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented pipe open is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.
A statement-level open whose return value is ignored is a diagnostic-only unchecked-open finding at the call span.
An independently authored open guarded by or die is not an unchecked-open finding.
A project-shaped store that checks both open and close with or die is not an unchecked finding.
File-level suppression of the governed unchecked rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented unchecked open is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.
Existing POD missing a required =head1 DESCRIPTION section is a diagnostic-only documentation finding at the first POD span.
An independently authored complete POD block with NAME and DESCRIPTION is not a finding.
A project-shaped module with complete POD sections is not a finding.
File-level suppression of the governed POD rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A file with no POD at all is outside this rule, which only checks existing POD, and is not a finding.
An integer literal with a silent leading-zero octal reading is a diagnostic-only finding at the literal span.
An independently authored plain decimal literal is not a leading-zero finding.
A project-shaped helper returning a plain decimal value is not a leading-zero finding.
File-level suppression of the governed leading-zero rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
Plain zero and explicit hex literals are exempt and are not leading-zero findings.
A bareword under strict is a preview-candidate finding at the bareword span, never automatic.
An independently authored quoted string is not an unquoted-bareword finding.
A project-shaped fat-comma hash key is auto-quoted and is not an unquoted-bareword finding.
File-level suppression of the governed bareword rule removes that finding; stripping it restores the same rule.
A commented bareword is not a finding; comment text does not inherit a positive.
